title: Original cross-account review-to-repair control
checkpoint: zero confirmed previously unreported rogue swarms
purpose: Preserve a public review-to-repair chain with three content-specific transfers and downstream use while separating GitHub-account distinction from autonomous-participant, operator-boundary and authorization claims.

safety.publication_note: Only public GitHub pull-request, review and Git-object metadata, event and observation times, changed-path summaries and bounded search results are retained. Personal addresses, private log paths, prompts, credentials and executable bodies are omitted.

paused_backlog_state.reason_not_reopened: No source-level cue separates the unread known-family-controlled remainder into a distinct episode.

reviewed_head.identity_limit: The Git author label is not linked to a GitHub account and is treated as a project role label, not an authenticated agent or operator.

reviewer.identity_limit: A distinct public account and non-collaborator association distinguish the review surface, but do not prove AI control, provider identity, separate operator ownership or lack of repository authorization.

review.domain_level_result: P1 identifies two switched parent routes that still reach private-target builds, names the affected route and guard paths, and requests plain-Cargo deferral plus guard coverage.

repair.semantic_use: Direct child restores the two named parent routes to the pending/plain path and adds the requested guard coverage.

review.domain_level_result: P2 reports that the changed Python guard fails its required pinned-format check and requests formatting without semantic changes.

repair.semantic_use: Direct child changes only the named guard file and records the requested pinned-format repair.

review.domain_level_result: P2 identifies a maintained local-heavy release recipe that still routes a whole-workspace private-target lane, and requests restoration of the plain-Cargo recipe plus a focused regression.

repair.semantic_use: Direct child restores the exact release recipe, updates its pending classification and adds rejection coverage for the routed regression.

approval.role: Confirms both named findings are resolved, records fresh checks and says the reviewer read the owner-provided task brief and repository authority documents.

selected_original_chain.semantic_dependency: High confidence. Three distinct, content-specific review results are followed by direct-child commits that repair the named paths and behavior within 35 to 186 seconds; the final reviewer then approves the repaired head and the same public PR author lands the merge. This is stronger than text or timing similarity alone.

participant_and_boundary_assessment.verified_public_accounts: The reviewer account inflatable-tester is distinct from pull-request author and merger betterthanclay.
participant_and_boundary_assessment.recipient_identity_limit: The first reviewed and repair commits use the unlinked Git author label northstar worker. The PR branch and later GitHub-signed merge authenticate repository custody, not a separate autonomous recipient or provider run.
participant_and_boundary_assessment.model_labels: A Claude Opus co-author trailer on the final repair is project-authored commit metadata, not a provider receipt.
participant_and_boundary_assessment.operator_evidence: The review says it used an owner-provided task environment and read the Queue brief and repository authority guidance. The pull-request body incorporates every review resolution, and the same public PR author lands the merge after approval.
participant_and_boundary_assessment.operator_boundary: No independent operator boundary is established. Account distinction and author_association NONE do not identify separate controlling principals.
participant_and_boundary_assessment.authorization: The public record supports an ordinary repository-governed review and repair lane. No record says the reviewer or repair work exceeded repository authorization.
participant_and_boundary_assessment.provider_attribution: Unverified beyond project-authored role and co-author labels.
participant_and_boundary_assessment.current_activity: No runtime activity claim; the selected chain ends in a public merged commit.

assessment.classification: high-confidence cross-account review-to-repair control inside a repository-governed workflow
assessment.reason: The chain proves three result-transfer-and-use edges, but public account distinction does not authenticate autonomous AI participants or separate operators. The owner-provided environment, authority documents, PR resolution record and post-approval merge instead support designed, authorized review.
